analyst_view.overall: A mid-table meeting: Utrecht are 13th with 12 points and NEC 14th with 11, and the two sides have conceded 50 league goals between them. NEC beat Omonia 3-1 in the Europa League on Thursday but are eight league games without a win; Utrecht lost 4-2 at Telstar last week and coach Anthony Correia promised tighter discipline. NEC's Perr Schuurs is a doubt after going off on Thursday, and Tobias Storm has a slight hamstring issue.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, trimmed slightly by past meetings. Both defences are leaky (Utrecht have conceded 31 in 11 games), NEC have conceded in each of their last seven matches, and NEC may be without centre-back Schuurs after Thursday. We lean a little above the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, split almost evenly. NEC keep a lot of the ball (over 60% at Heerenveen) but one preview says they struggle to create clear chances, while Utrecht are stronger at home. These roughly balance, so we stay with the site.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards, cut by NEC's recent games and referee Erwin Blank's record. Correia said he wants more discipline and intensity after the Telstar defeat, and NEC arrive with tired legs from Thursday, which can bring late fouls. We lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, raised by NEC's recent volume. That fits NEC's possession game and Utrecht's home record, and we found nothing to push it either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. With Utrecht's Artem Stepanov leading the league with five goals and NEC's Chery and Linssen their main threats, the site's number looks about right.
